dedupe_keys.name: high dimensional bayesian inference for structural health monitoring of lock gates mississippi river lock 27

description: A statistical method, described in a December 2018 arXiv preprint by Matthew Parno, Devin O'Connor and Matthew Smith, for monitoring the structural health of navigation lock gates that are operating past their design life. Contents: a high-dimensional Bayesian inference problem joins noisy real-time strain observations with a detailed finite element model of the gate; Karhunen-Loève decompositions, stochastic differential equation forms of Gaussian processes and Kalman smoothing make the cost scale linearly with the number of observations. Quasi-periodic Gaussian processes capture thermal effects on strain, and gate boundary conditions, where damage such as lost contact appears, are inferred with Gaussian process priors. Coverage: a synthetic example and real data from Mississippi River Lock 27 near St. Louis, Missouri; nearly 1.4 million parameters were characterised in under an hour on a desktop computer. Format and access: free preprint; no code release was found. Licence and cost: free to read. Caveats: one lock and a research method, not an operational tool. Useful as a digital twin and resilience building block that turns gate sensor data into condition states for lock failure and closure models. It relates to the Upper Mississippi navigation pools bed sediment data in the catalogue.
